newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Tupolev plans to sell 25 planes this year.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Tupolev plans to sell 25 planes this year.

text.p: Russian plane designer Aviatsionny Nauchno-Technicheski Kompleks Tupolev plans to sell 25 passenger aircraft this year, the head of the company said on Wednesday.
Chief executive Valentin Klimov told a news conference that five of these planes would be produced under an agreement with Egypt's Kato group.
"Five Tupolev-204 jets, powered by Rolls-Royce engines, must be produced by the end of this year," Klimov said.
Last year Kato group, which is diversifying into aviation, said it would buy 200 Tu-204 jets powered by Rolls-Royce engines and with Honeywell -Allied Signal avionics by 2001.
Russian officials would not say how much the deal was worth, though the Middle East Digest magazine said it was worth $450 million.

"The first of these five aircraft is almost completed," Klimov said. The Russian goverment has not yet given financial guarantees that Kato's cash advance would be returned if the planes are not delivered, he noted.
"We hope to get the guarantees soon," he added.
Klimov said the company had another 30 orders for Tu-204s, but did not say from whom.
The Tupolev Komplex comprises a Moscow-based design bureau, test-flight base and several experimental production plants.

Tupolev in turn has agreements with plane-makers such as AO Aviastar in the Central Russian city of Ulyanovsk, Kazan avaiation plant in Tatarstan, AO Aviakor in Samara and Kiev aviation plant in Ukraine.
These plane-makers produce the planes and share the proceeds from any sales with Tupolev.
